sec: High Colored Urine — approach flowchart · p742

items.q: In the printed approach, which action carries the number 3?
items.exp: The flowchart is numbered 1. Dipstick test, 2. Centrifugation of urine (1600 rpm × 5 minutes), 3. Biopsy, 4. Sample undisturbed for 3–6 hours — the fourth step sits on the right-hand, high-coloured branch. (Book p742)

items.q: Of the three branches under 'Causes', the nephrological (9%) branch is the only one left without a named disease on this page.
opts: True — urological names carcinoma bladder and hematological names intravascular hemolysis
False — nephrological names glomerulonephritis in brackets
False — the hematological branch also lacks an example
True — and the nephrological share is printed as 1%
items.exp: Causes: urological (90%) — carcinoma bladder (m/c); Nephrological (9%) with nothing printed under it; Hematological (1%) — intravascular hemolysis. (Book p742)

items.q: Fill up: The glomerular-hematuria box requires ≥40% dysmorphic RBCs, ≥5% acanthocytes, or a ______ RBC cast with proteinuria.
items.exp: Printed criteria: ≥40 % dysmorphic RBCs / ≥5 % acanthocytes / single RBC cast + proteinuria → 3. Biopsy. (Book p742)

items.q: Tea-coloured urine shows blood on dipstick; after centrifugation the supernatant is clear, but microscopy reports 25% dysmorphic RBCs, no casts and no proteinuria. Following the flowchart, the next step is:
opts: Treat it as a urological cause and send radiological investigation — USG abdomen and CT
Proceed to biopsy, since any dysmorphic cells make it glomerular
Leave the sample undisturbed for 3–6 hours and re-examine the colour
Measure serum complement, because the picture fits nephrological disease
items.exp: The glomerular criteria need ≥40% dysmorphic cells, ≥5% acanthocytes, or a single RBC cast plus proteinuria; none is met, so the left branch runs to 'urological cause → radiological Ix (USG abdomen, CT)'. (Book p742)

items.q: The opening line lists all of these presentations of high-coloured urine EXCEPT:
items.exp: 'Can be hematuria, red, pink, tea, cola colored urine' — a milky white urine belongs to the pale/white row of the appearance table on p740, not to this line. (Book p742)
